sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house fast in Rome, GA?
sections.html:
Rome owners can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer for the house as it is. Each has a place. Which one wins for you depends on the age of the house, how much repair work it needs, and whether anyone besides you, such as a tenant or a co-heir, has a say.

Rome has a large rental share, which affects how houses change hands. Census QuickFacts lists the owner-occupied rate at 49.2%, so about half of the housing is rented. A plain cash sale tends to suit landlords, heirs of a family house and owners of an older home better than a long listing does.

  • Cash offer: one walk-through, an offer on the spot or soon after, no repairs and a closing date that fits your schedule.
  • Agent sale: the best chance at full market value for a house in good order, with showings, an inspection and a lender's timetable.
  • Private sale: you skip the agent fee and take on the pricing, the contract and the buyer's questions yourself.

Write down what each route would leave in your pocket after fees, repairs and the months of taxes, insurance and utilities you pay while waiting.

sections.h2: Where is Rome, Georgia, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Rome is the seat of Floyd County in northwest Georgia, sitting where the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers join to form the Coosa. The New Georgia Encyclopedia places it inside a triangle formed by Atlanta, Birmingham and Chattanooga and says the city was founded in 1834 on the site of a large Cherokee settlement called Head of Coosa.

Transportation and cotton drove the early economy. Steamboats reached Rome in 1836, a railroad charter followed in 1839, and Norfolk Southern still runs a freight yard in the city. The Clocktower was built in 1871, Cherokee Baptist Female College, later Shorter University, opened in 1873, and Berry College was founded in 1902 on the north edge of the city.

Textiles and carpet shaped the twentieth century, and the encyclopedia reports that both have largely faded. General Electric and Georgia Power's Plant Hammond arrived in the 1950s. The encyclopedia says health care and education now carry more weight, listing three hospitals, two public colleges and two private ones, along with manufacturers such as Suzuki Manufacturing of America and the North American headquarters of Pirelli Tire. Rome and Floyd County were designated one of Georgia's metropolitan statistical areas in 2003.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Rome homes and incomes?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts estimates Rome's population at 38,934 for July 1, 2025, compared with 37,713 in the 2020 census and 36,303 in 2010. Growth since the April 2020 estimates base is 2.7%, far below the 24.8% shown for Perry and 28.0% for Pooler over the same stretch.

  • Tenure and value: an owner-occupied rate of 49.2% and a median owner-occupied value of $234,300 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Monthly costs: median owner costs of $1,526 with a mortgage, and a median gross rent of $1,032.
  • Households and size: 14,983 households across 31.68 square miles of land.

A median household income of $54,435 in 2024 dollars gives a sense of local affordability. Health care and social assistance is the largest receipts line in QuickFacts for 2022, at $1,596,086 thousand, which fits the encyclopedia's description of Rome as a regional medical center.

sections.h2: What do Rome and Floyd County rules mean for a house sale?
sections.html:
Rome and Floyd County share a Unified Land Development Code, and the city lists it with a 2040 Comprehensive Plan on its Board of Adjustments page. Planning staff take appointments for questions about a property, a project or a request.

The Board of Adjustments hears appeals of an administrative decision, special exceptions, hardship variances and flood protection variances. It meets on the third Thursday of each month at 2:30 p.m. in the upstairs Commission Chambers at City Hall, 601 Broad Street. Applications are due by 5:00 p.m. on the 25th of the month, and a request filed by that deadline is considered no sooner than two months later.

  • Special exceptions: relief from setbacks, building height, lot width, street frontage, buffers, signs and parking requirements.
  • Hardship variances: granted only for extraordinary property conditions such as size, shape or topography, or for unnecessary hardship, and never for a condition the applicant created, a use the zoning does not allow, or added dwelling units.
  • Waiting period: after a denial, a request for the same property cannot return for 12 months unless the board shortens the wait.

If your house has a nonconforming addition, a garage apartment or a setback problem, raise it with planning staff before a buyer's survey does. A cash buyer can accept the problem, but a lender may refuse to.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Floyd County assessment on a Rome house?
sections.html:
You file a written appeal with the Floyd County Board of Assessors within 45 days of the mailing date on the notice of assessment. The county says an appeal can rest on taxability, uniformity, value or a denial of a homestead exemption.

The Board of Assessors and its appraisal staff review the file and decide whether to raise, lower or keep the value. If the value stays, the appeal moves to the Board of Equalization automatically. If the value changes, the owner has 21 days to appeal the new figure in writing. The table lays out the four formal routes the county describes.

RouteGrounds allowedKey timing from the county
Board of EqualizationAny groundsAppeal within 45 days of the notice; a decision can go to Superior Court within 30 days
Hearing OfficerValue or uniformity only; non-homesteaded parcel valued over $1 millionCounty has 90 days to review
Binding arbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer has 45 days after the county's acknowledgment to submit a certified appraisal
Superior CourtAny groundsAppeal within 45 days of the notice; fees apply

Source: Floyd County Board of Assessors, Appeals page.

sections.h2: What is recorded when a Rome sale closes?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the clerk of superior court, and the real estate transfer tax must be paid first. The Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority describes the tax as an excise tax on the sale of real property and has the filer complete Form PT-61 online, then print one copy to file with the deed.

Rome houses are recorded with the Floyd County clerk of superior court. Ask your closing attorney or title company to name the party responsible for the tax in your contract and to confirm the rate that applies to your deed.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Rome house?
sections.html:
Cash is worth pricing out in these Rome situations:

  • A landlord selling a rental with tenants in place or with damage left by a departing tenant.
  • A family house near downtown that needs a roof, wiring or foundation work.
  • An estate in which heirs live in different states and cannot manage repairs.
  • A seller with a mortgage in arrears who needs a closing date before the lender's deadline.

Ask for a written offer, an explanation of who pays closing costs and a closing date. Then compare it with a listing's likely net.

faqs.q: Is Rome, Georgia, a renter-heavy market?
faqs.a: Yes, more than most. Census QuickFacts shows an owner-occupied rate of 49.2% for 2020 to 2024, which means about half of the housing is rented. That affects who buys, and it explains why many local sellers are landlords.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Floyd County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date of the notice of assessment, and the appeal must be in writing to the Board of Assessors. If the value changes after review, you get 21 days to appeal the new figure to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Who handles variance requests in Rome?
faqs.a: The Rome and Floyd County Board of Adjustments does. It meets on the third Thursday of each month at City Hall, and applications are due by 5:00 p.m. on the 25th. Planning staff will schedule an appointment to talk through a request.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rome house that has code or permit problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell any buyer about the problem. A cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands, while a lender may require the issue to be fixed or cleared first. Planning staff can tell you what the city's records show for the address.

faqs.q: What do I file to record a deed in Rome?
faqs.a: The deed and a Form PT-61 go to the Floyd County clerk of superior court, and the transfer tax must be paid before recording. The PT-61 is filled out online with the Georgia clerks' authority, and your closing attorney normally files it.
